prompt: Two feuding families on either side of the river, each with their own manor, farms and guards.

plan.notes: One estate on each bank of the river, no bridge. Lots are written west bank first, then east bank. Buildings are laid out in one region for now; the bank split and family colours are carried as pending rules.

zones.label: The two estates
zones.notes: Straddles the river: west-bank lots go west of the water, east-bank lots east. Guard towers face the water; no shared market or tavern.

lots.label: west bank manor
lots.brief: Seat of the first family on the west bank, in its own colours and banners; windows and balcony face the river and the rival manor.

lots.label: east bank manor
lots.brief: Seat of the second family on the east bank, in contrasting colours and banners; faces the first manor across the water.

rules.label: Family colours and banners
rules.notes: West bank buildings in one family's colours and banners, east bank in a contrasting set; the two palettes must not mix.

rules.label: Mirrored estates on each bank
rules.notes: The two banks mirror each other across the river, with manors facing and towers on the water edge.

waits.words: Each family's own colours and banners: palette rules come with a later Architect release; the estates are built first in the rustic style and the colours are applied when they can be.
Strict mirrored halves on each bank: shape rules come with a later release; the lots are written with bank notes and the layout is not guaranteed to mirror yet.

answer.summary: The Feuding Banks is one farming settlement of 14 buildings across a river: a manor, farmhouse, barn, guard tower, two retainers' cottages and a barracks for each family, with no bridge and no shared market. It is placed near the largest river and sized at 64x64 so both banks fit. Family colours and the strict mirrored layout are kept as pending rules until Architect supports them.
